National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
947 AM EDT Fri Oct 30 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
No significant changes to the forecast for today.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Very warm conditions today, with seasonable temperatures an dry 
conditions for Halloween weekend. 

- 2) Rain chances will likely hold off until the second half of next 
week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Very warm conditions today, with seasonable 
temperatures an dry conditions for Halloween weekend. 

Latest satellite and observations indicate a weak cold front is
beginning to enter the area from the northwest. Clouds over the
Alleghenies are dissipating late this morning as dry air advects
in, so expect mostly sunny skies across the region. The 
gradient between the departing front and incoming high pressure 
will yield west to northwest downsloping winds up to 25 mph. 

Expect above normal temperatures in the low to mid 70s (60s 
mountains). Locations south of DC and down toward 
Charlottesville have a shot to briefly touch 80 degrees given 
the very dry air ahead of and behind the front. 

High pressure will builds across the region into the weekend,
bringing cooler temperature. Expect much more seasonable 
weather for both Halloween Saturday and Sunday. Highs both days 
will push into the 60s with overnight lows in the 30s and 40s. 
Expect more sunshine Saturday compared to Sunday given the high 
nearby. Cloud cover will increase Sunday afternoon and night as 
a shortwave trough passes south of the area. This trough may 
touch off a shower or two Sunday night although most will remain
dry given the residual mid-level dry air with high pressure 
nearby. 


KEY MESSAGE 2...Rain chances will likely hold off until the second 
half of next week.

Models are arriving at better agreement that mid level ridging will 
build along the east coast during the first half of next week. A 
shortwave trough may cross the area Monday before the ridge takes 
hold, and there is still an outside chance a few showers could occur 
as it passes. At a minimum, expect cloudier conditions. Temperatures 
will likely climb Tuesday and Wednesday, with highs reaching the 70s 
for many areas.

A deep trough will approach from the west the second half of the 
week. A low pressure system will likely be lurking over the Bahamas, 
and some guidance suggests this system, or at least some of its 
moisture, could be swept northward into the Mid Atlantic ahead of 
the trough. While the details remain uncertain, expect increasing 
rain chances in the Wednesday through Friday period.

&&

.AVIATION /13Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
Prevailing VFR conditions are forecast to continue through the 
upcoming weekend as high pressure builds into the region. A dry cold 
front will cross the terminals later this morning and into the 
afternoon leading to some passing mid and high level cloud cover. 
Winds will kick up in the wake of the front out of the west and 
northwest with gusts between 20 to 25 kts. Highest gusts will be at 
terminals near the waters and along the ridges. Winds will gradually 
diminish Saturday morning into Saturday afternoon as high pressure 
settles overhead. Northerly winds will prevail through Saturday 
night at less than 10 kts. 

VFR conditions are expected Sunday into Monday as high pressure 
continues to meander nearby. Winds will turn to the south and 
southeast and less than 15 kts. Significant weather is unlikely 
Monday and Tuesday as high pressure moves eastward. However, some 
low chances of sub-VFR ceilings exist Monday or Monday night 
depending on how the weather pattern evolves.

&&

.MARINE...
A weak/dry cold front will push across the waters this morning with 
high pressure building south over the region this weekend. SCA 
conditions are expected from late this morning through early 
Saturday morning, especially over the open waters. This is largely 
due in part to northerly channeling. Winds diminish below SCA level 
Saturday morning before falling back below sub-SCA levels Saturday 
afternoon. Sub-SCA conditions look to continue Sunday into Monday 
with wedging high pressure meandering nearby. Winds will change to 
the south and southeast as high pressure sits north and east of the 
area. Speeds will generally be between 5-10 kts. Showers may impact 
the middle and southern waters Monday afternoon as a wave of low 
pressure approaches from the south and west. Better chances for 
rain by the end of next week.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Offshore flow develops behind a cold frontal passage this morning 
allowing tidal anomalies to drop over the next few days. Winds turn 
back to the south Sunday afternoon leading to modest rises in 
anomalies heading into early next week.
